text:
[LNUL.4.3] **A `where` clause fires iff it evaluates to `true`.** Both `false`
and `null` (unknown) do **not** fire. Net effect: **a missing value never
causes a rule to fire** — neither positively (`s.state > 85`) nor through
negation (`not (s.state > 85)`) — unless the author handles absence explicitly
([LNUL.5]). This is the safe, auditable default: *don't act on what you don't
know.*

idris.name: lnul_4_3__admits_closed
idris.note: The where site: a match test fires iff it evaluates to true, so the absent value does not match -- failing CLOSED, as the clause rules. Identical to the guard site everywhere the value evaluated.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__sites_agree_when_evaluable
idris.note: The two sites agree on EVERY evaluable value. This is the half that makes the disagreement dangerous rather than obvious: no test over evaluable inputs can tell the sites apart.

idris.name: lnul_4_8__sites_disagree_on_absent
idris.note: The witness that the two sites take OPPOSITE dispositions of the one absent value: `Not (True = False)` between the where site and the guard site -- the row this clause writes for the where test, against the row [LNUL.4.8] writes for the guard.

idris.name: iret_7_6__admits_join
idris.note: A positive node's join relation over the extended token, the candidate last: admitted iff the evaluated test answers true.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__admits
idris.note: A positive node admits a pair iff its tests answer true: false, null and a trap all decline, which is the clause's 'fires iff it evaluates to true' over the four answers.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__admits_only_true
idris.note: Only true is admitted, over all four answers.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__null_comparison_never_fires
idris.note: The clause's hot / cool pair quantified over every operator and every other operand: a comparison with a null operand fires neither positively nor under not.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__undecided_neither_admits_nor_passes
idris.note: The positive half of the clause's safety collapse: an answer that is neither true nor false (null, or a trap) is not admitted.

idris.name: iret_7_5_1__probe_positive
idris.note: THE PROBE IS TRANSPARENT AT A POSITIVE NODE, for an anchor wherever it stands in the test list: the bucket, tested by the other tests, is exactly what the whole list admits, traps included. The clause's 'probing on one first cannot change whether the pair passes'.

idris.name: iret_7_6__node_join
idris.note: The relation a node reads from its test: a positive node admits a pair answering true, a `no` node counts a candidate as a blocker unless it answers false. One test, two relations -- RLOW.5.3's 'the same join tests as the positive form'.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__admits_and
idris.note: A positive node admits an `and` iff it admits both sides.

idris.name: lnul_4_3__extends_iff_true
idris.note: A positive node extends a token by exactly the candidates answering true: every extension it passes is one, and every one is passed.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_1__test_of
idris.note: A `where` fires iff it evaluates to `true`: the timed test admits on `true` alone, and `false` and `null` do not -- `iret_7_6__admits_join`'s reading, which a `dwell` that reads `null` (no stamp) and a `null` slot it is compared with both reach.

idris.name: rdsc_4a_8_2_2__null_condition_withholds
idris.note: A `where` that evaluates to `null` does not fire: `dwell >= null` admits nothing, at either pump. Executed.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__decide
idris.note: The decision: a positive pattern fires on true ([LNUL.4.3]); a `no` pattern is blocked unless false, a trap included -- [LNUL.4.7] blocks on true and on null and says nothing of a trap, as Rete/NetworkAnswer.idr's `iret_7_6__node_join` has it.

idris.name: lnul_4_7__decide_is_node_join
idris.note: The node's decision is NetworkAnswer's `iret_7_6__node_join` of the V5 test.
